Definition: from G1909 and G5342; to bear upon (or further), i.e. adduce (personally or judicially (accuse, inflict)), superinduce:--add, bring (against), take.
BiblicalUsage: Epiphero means to bring upon, to bring against — to adduce a charge. Paul asks, is God unrighteous who taketh vengeance, if our unrighteousness commend the righteousness of God? And Michael the archangel, when disputing with the devil, durst not bring against him a railing accusation.
TheologicalSignificance: If an archangel would not rail, I should not either, and the restraint of Michael rebukes my readiness to accuse.
